# Assembled application owner

The reference is unchanged Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. [The independent fixture](released-application.json), SHA-256 `769f45cc37495d82b1930db588567a63af601ea94b75e5b1a5145aae1ede9a8b`, contains eight application workflows and 56 GTK/store/clipboard/widget states. The external observer invokes the real released application activation, registered actions, buttons, buffers and shutdown; every imported reference module is checked against that commit. No released handler is replaced. The temporary observer remains under ignored `tmp/` and is not part of native checks.

The separate [command fixture and evidence](application-commands-evidence.md) add twenty states and four layouts; [continuation evidence](application-continuation-evidence.md) adds 28 states and two layouts; [Live workspace evidence](live-workspace-evidence.md) adds 22 states and four layouts. The [Live editor comparison](live-editor-evidence.md) adds four workflows/21 states for held finalization, manual edits and real storage/copy failures. The shared native harness runs fifteen workflows/147 states through `make linux-application-test`, with acknowledged shutdown for each. Command, continuation and Live workspace Make targets depend on that single run. The eight-workflow fixture above remains unchanged.

The [compact comparison](compact-workspace-evidence.md) selects eleven further workflows/22 layout-and-reopen states into separate fresh sessions through `make linux-compact-workspace-test`. It does not duplicate the default fifteen-workflow run. Actual pending provider operations cover minimum/narrow/wide/2× layouts, selected-versus-empty finalization and a repair to root History refresh ordering. The compact fixture retains seven complete speech requests and seven Codex inputs; existing application fixtures remain unchanged.

The [joined image comparison](application-images-evidence.md) selects four fresh sessions/seventeen states and four full-window images through native `make linux-screenshot-test`. It joins the real bridge, app-launched Tensaku and annotation helper to simultaneous main recording and exact image context, plus preparation failure before audio starts. These sessions do not duplicate the default fifteen-workflow/147-state run.

The native comparison constructs `ApplicationDesktop`, its real settings/setup, capture, Live, review, pending decisions, History, Meeting, personalization and title owners. Speech travels through the production capture service, recorder/session and compatible HTTP client. A separate native PCM process supplies synthetic audio; a separate native Codex process speaks the real JSONL protocol. User credentials and physical devices are unavailable. Actual provider requests, saved History, Notes recovery and private clipboard bytes are compared.

The [assembled provider comparison](application-providers-evidence.md) adds six fresh-session scenarios/twenty states and twelve full-page layouts through `make linux-provider-settings-test`. Real keyring/Codex/HTTP/PCM peers verify Apply, service readiness, active-recording rejection, catalog cancellation, offline recovery and reopened choices. It caught a false discovery error after successful Apply. All twelve complete images match the release, and the Make target runs with interpreter traps unused. These scenarios do not duplicate the default fifteen-workflow run.

The [assembled management comparison](application-management-evidence.md) adds three fresh sessions/69 states and fifteen images through `make linux-conversation-management-test`. It joins actual title/sidebar/dialog callbacks to stored titles, edited drafts, replies, merge/delete transactions, and recording/rewrite/privacy guards. All images match the release, and Python/uv traps remain unused. The default fifteen-workflow/147-state run is unchanged.

The [assembled prompt comparison](application-prompts-evidence.md) adds four sessions with separate-process restarts, 53 states and fourteen exact images through `make linux-prompt-test`. Real recordings and external provider requests verify frozen instructions, manual drafts and the next recording's saved prompt. Root editor/style controls, file conflicts and malformed-config preservation match; a missing initial Incognito state is repaired. The existing editor owner also runs with Python/uv traps unused. The default fifteen-workflow/147-state run remains unchanged.

The workflows cover completed dictation with automatic and fallback titles; navigation to History, Settings, Meeting, Personalization and the latest conversation; Command preview/explicit copy acceptance; Notes edits/explicit copy acceptance; review blocking a second recording; and closing during recording. The settings repair starts without speech credentials, changes the actual provider form, records successfully and acknowledges the startup callout. Two exit cases require Live Once to become disabled, including when `config.json` is replaced by an unwritable destination. Shutdown must acknowledge audio/provider cleanup before returning: child processes and ephemeral Codex workspaces are gone, cancelled recordings have no audio or History row, and the required platform-close action has run.

A separate session-bus connection observes both actual recording-status signals. Each active capture phase uses an actually received matching state/shell pair; asynchronous replay can advance to recording while a clipboard read completes, so phase samples are selected from the observed messages rather than assuming transport timing. Elapsed seconds and audio level are marked `sampled`; their wire types and bounds have separate independent projection tests. Generated entry identifiers use a per-workflow mapping shared by History and review messages. Private paths, generated audio names and provider timings use the existing capture observer's documented normalization. Provider prompts and uploaded audio remain exact.

The assembled comparison failed before these owner repairs: a controller-written fallback prevented automatic title jobs from running; the widget had wrong recording/provider/mode text, stale preview and motion settings; explicit shutdown did not consume Live Once; and provider repair prematurely erased the retained startup callout while its acknowledgement left a stale widget review. Title completion now goes to the real title owner, recording publication follows the live preview update, and shutdown disarms Once even when persistence fails. Service readiness and the released startup-error annotation are separate, so provider repair enables recording and explicit Retry acknowledges the callout. The existing standalone capture comparisons also use the real title owner instead of reproducing its fallback behavior.

The private runner isolates DISPLAY, HOME/XDG state, accessibility/session buses, network, PID namespace and devices. Run this check with `$OFFSCREEN_SESSION_ROOT/application-tools` first in PATH, `MLUVA_DISABLE_GLOBAL_SHORTCUT=1` and UTC timezone; the test guards those boundaries before installing its synthetic audio/Codex executables. The disabled portal matches this fixture's released observer. The separate [application-shortcut comparison](application-shortcuts-evidence.md) exercises actual registration, key actions and target delivery with that variable absent. This check requires the existing native peers, GTK/Pango versions recorded by the fixture, and the `dev/run-isolated-browser.sh` environment. Both applications use unique test application IDs and `NON_UNIQUE`; this is not a single-instance/bootstrap comparison. There is no interpreter dependency in the native test.

This is a bounded assembled-graph comparison. Separate [shortcut evidence](application-shortcuts-evidence.md) and [screenshot evidence](application-screenshots-evidence.md) now exercise root-owned portal registration, picker/editor ownership and Stop waiting for images. Required `ApplicationPlatform` actions are limited to compositor presentation and distribution shutdown. Executable/bootstrap, real Omarchy widget/selection, physical keys/devices, narrated text boxes, all provider/settings races, every command/management/error path, packaging, Python removal and performance acceptance remain required. All complete-workflow parity rows remain Pending and the installed app/widget remain 1.6.0. GTK 4.14 enables the same accessibility announcement API used by the reference.
